title: Security groups and network ACLs: two filters with different jobs

videos.script: A packet that reaches the shop meets two filters, and they work in different ways. {{two}} The first is the network ACL. It sits at the edge of a subnet. Its rules are numbered, they can allow or deny, and the first one that matches decides. It remembers nothing, so every reply needs a rule of its own. {{acl}} The second is the security group. It sits on each machine's network interface. It can only allow. And it remembers: a reply to a connection it let in goes back out by itself. {{sg}} A security group can name another group as its source. So the database trusts the application, and the application trusts the load balancer, whatever their addresses are. {{chain}} You will build those rules, then walk three packets through both filters by hand. One gets in. One is dropped at the edge. One passes every address check and is still refused. {{walks}} moto stores every rule and filters nothing, so the walking is yours to do. On AWS, two tools check it for you, and this lesson names them. {{end}}
